candidate.uc_full_name: Incremental Application of the GREEN Framework
candidate.requirement: Retain provenance and uncertainty for the legacy baseline when comparing it with later measurements.
candidate.workaround: Keep baseline source, observed value, and comparison as controller metadata; do not label unknown telemetry as zero.
candidate.impact: Baseline comparisons remain contextual and cannot be reconstructed from current Energy Object leaves alone.

decisions.rationale: The baseline comparison and vendor source are controller-side provenance; existing data-source-accuracy identities cover measured, estimated, and static source quality, and no interoperable device baseline field is required by the event text.

candidate.uc_full_name: Selective reduction of energy consumption in network parts proportional to traffic levels
candidate.requirement: Relate traffic condition and service continuity to component power-state transitions.
candidate.workaround: Keep traffic-condition, traffic-action, and service-continuity in controller metadata; consume reported power and operational state separately.
candidate.impact: A snapshot does not by itself encode why a component entered low power.

decisions.rationale: Traffic condition and service continuity are controller policy inputs; the device model already exposes current power and operational state, so no additional energy leaf is required.

candidate.requirement: Distinguish a direct target measurement from an external meter correlated with an uninstrumented target.
candidate.workaround: Use explicit metering/powering relationships and preserve target-direct-measurement=unknown as controller metadata.
candidate.impact: The external reading is visible, but attribution and direct-versus-indirect status require controller context.

decisions.rationale: The model has measurement-local and directional metering/powering relationships. The target's unknown direct measurement remains correctly represented as unknown controller context.

candidate.uc_full_name: Consideration of other domains for obtention of end-to-end metrics
candidate.requirement: Normalize domain inputs and retain the composition and boundary-guard provenance of an end-to-end value.
candidate.workaround: Keep source-domain values, normalization, shared-boundary decision, and composed result with controller provenance.
candidate.impact: An aggregate Energy Object is visible, but the operation and contributing domain lineage are not in the snapshot.

decisions.rationale: Aggregating/aggregated-by and power/energy leaves represent the objects and readings; normalization, boundary guards, and lineage are processing provenance, not missing device state.

candidate.uc_full_name: Dynamic adjustment of network element throughput according to traffic levels in wireless transport networks
candidate.requirement: Associate a radio throughput profile and traffic condition with observed link power.
candidate.workaround: Retain traffic condition, throughput profile, and service-continuity as controller metadata alongside YANG power-state and measurement leaves.
candidate.impact: The current operational snapshot has no traffic-profile context for a link power value.

decisions.rationale: Throughput profile and traffic condition are network-control context outside this energy-object operational model; the controller can retain them as metadata.

candidate.requirement: Relate delivery strategy and cache placement to observed energy values without asserting a standardized control protocol.
candidate.workaround: Keep delivery-strategy and cache-placement as explicitly simulator/controller metadata.
candidate.impact: Energy Objects can be measured, but delivery choices are not part of their current operational data.

decisions.rationale: Delivery strategy and cache placement are application/controller context; the current energy objects already carry the observed power values.

candidate.requirement: Relate AP power-state and PoE power changes to coverage and recovery-delay constraints.
candidate.workaround: Use power-state and explicit enabling/metering/powering edges; keep coverage and recovery-delay constraints as controller metadata.
candidate.impact: Power state is represented, while the service constraint that governs mode choice is not.

decisions.rationale: The generic operational power-state leaf plus enabling, metering, and powering relationships represent the device state and topology; coverage and recovery-delay constraints are controller policy.

candidate.requirement: Compare energy measurements over a defined interval and distinguish interval energy from cumulative counters.
candidate.workaround: Keep raw counters and interval labels in controller metadata; do not aggregate values without compatible interval and reset semantics.
candidate.impact: The leaf is cumulative and its declared units conflict with its description; interval boundaries are not explicit in the current snapshot.
candidate.example_runtime_value: eo-upstream-meter=80 Wh interval; eo-server-b=20 Wh interval

schema_evidence: units statement declares Watt-hours; prose description also mentions mWh
decisions.rationale: The existing operational cumulative counter can be sampled and differenced by the controller; the controller records retrieval timestamps and can mark counter decreases/reset uncertainty incomplete. The machine-readable units statement declares Watt-hours; its conflicting prose is an editorial clarification candidate, not an unrepresentable node.

candidate.requirement: Preserve telemetry history and distinguish optimized, legacy, and unknown capability classifications.
candidate.workaround: Keep collected snapshots and classification provenance in the controller; retain unknown as unknown.
candidate.impact: Current power and accuracy identities are observable, but history and the use-case classification are controller-derived.

decisions.rationale: Existing data-source-accuracy identities cover measured/estimated/static/unavailable source quality; history and optimized/legacy classification are controller-derived.

candidate.uc_full_name: ISAC-enabled Energy-Aware Smart City Traffic Management
candidate.requirement: Relate sensing mode and energy-aware routing to the requirement that critical sensing remains active.
candidate.workaround: Keep sensing mode, traffic action, and critical-function status as controller metadata; observe power-state and measurements independently.
candidate.impact: Reported component power does not encode the sensing or critical-service context.

decisions.rationale: Sensing modes, traffic routing, and critical-function policy are application/controller semantics; hardware state, power, and aggregation relationships are available for the energy view.

candidate.requirement: Determine whether a measurement boundary is complete and whether a de-duplicated accounting result is authoritative.
candidate.workaround: Traverse explicit metering edges; retain raw measurements and report incomplete topology without an accounted total.
candidate.impact: Relationships expose topology, but completeness and accounting status are computed controller-side.

decisions.rationale: Existing directional metering relationships are sufficient to compute topology completeness and accounting status in the controller; no device-side completeness state is required.

candidate.requirement: Relate power-source and battery level to critical-service preservation and non-critical reduction.
candidate.workaround: Preserve power-source, battery-level, and service-priority as controller metadata; keep reported power-state separate.
candidate.impact: The operational snapshot does not carry the battery and service-priority context needed to interpret the transition.

schema_evidence: generic sensor data is feature-gated by hardware-sensor: True
hardware-sensor feature enabled in current Sysrepo: False
IANA hardware battery identity exists: True
decisions.rationale: A battery state-of-charge is a concrete UC 2.14 operational value demonstrated by U14-1 through U14-3. The active Energy Object schema has no typed state-of-charge leaf. RFC 8348 generic sensor-data is feature-gated (hardware-sensor is not enabled in the inspected Sysrepo module) and its `other` value plus display string does not identify state-of-charge as a machine-readable battery semantic.

gap.solution: Add a local experimental battery-state-of-charge container with explicit available/unknown/unavailable status and a bounded percentage leaf.

candidate.uc_full_name: Energy-Efficient Management of Distributed AI Training Workloads
candidate.requirement: Relate energy observations to scheduling window, active-node allocation, and data locality.
candidate.workaround: Keep workload schedule, traffic, compression, and placement in controller metadata.
candidate.impact: Power-state is visible, but workload context is not present in the device data model.

decisions.rationale: Scheduling windows, workload placement, and active-node policy are controller/application context; existing Energy Objects and power-state leaves expose the relevant device observations.

candidate.requirement: Represent a cross-layer dependency check and preserve QoS during coordinated low-power transitions.
candidate.workaround: Traverse enabling edges and retain dependency-check and QoS observations as controller metadata.
candidate.impact: The dependency relation is visible, but coordination progress and service outcome are controller-derived.

decisions.rationale: The enabling/enabled-by relationship models functional dependency; coordination progress and QoS policy remain controller-side decision context.

group_b_review.title: Reporting on Lifecycle Management
group_b_review.decision: NOT A GAP candidate based on available text
modeling_needs_from_text: lifecycle embedded-energy/carbon estimates for manufacturing, transport, recyclability, and end-of-life
location-based carbon factors and energy mix
backup-source identity and awareness of which backup is in use
vendor, datasheet, or database information ingestion
group_b_review.rationale: The draft describes lifecycle reporting inputs and external metadata but gives no concrete event sequence, collection timing, or interoperable device data contract. No lifecycle transitions or external-data behavior are invented.

group_b_review.title: Real-time Energy Metering of Virtualised or Cloud-native Network Functions
group_b_review.decision: NOT A GAP candidate based on available text
modeling_needs_from_text: real-time energy measurement for virtualized or cloud-native functions
metering across hardware and software layers
group_b_review.rationale: The draft states a high-level metering need but leaves GREEN requirements as TODO; it does not define virtual entity identity, host correlation, shared-energy attribution, migration behavior, or event timing.
